Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Test: big objects rise maximally to just above the topmost small object; small fall to floor.
# Check D1 with this rule manually via code:
def f(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    objs=comps_of(g)
    res=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    occ=[[False]*W for _ in range(H)]
    smalls=[];bigg=[]
    for c in objs:
        (smallsm if len(c)<8 else bigg).append(c)
    for cells in bigg+sorted(smalls,key=lambda c:len(c)):
        rmin=min(a for a,b in cells); rmax=max(a for a,b in cells)
        hgt=rmax-rmin+1
        if len(cells)>=8:      # rise to row 0 or stop on topmost small cell below
            sh=-rmin
            # check collision only within itself? assume none
            for a,b in cells:
                n=a+sh
                res[n][b]=g[a][b]; occ[n][b]=True
        else:
            best=0
            for s in range(1,H-hgt):
                if any(a+s>H-1 or occ[a+s][b] for a,b in cells):
                    break
                best=s
            sh=best
            for a,b in cells:
                n=a+sh
                res[n][b]=g[a][b]; occ[n][b]=True
    return res
for n in ('Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3'):
    print(n, f(G[n+' input'])==G[n+' output'])

def solve(g):
    H=len(g);W=len(g[0]);out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    cs=comps_of(g)
    # bigs first (any col-compatible order), then smalls by fall distance asc so far ones settle first
    ups=[c for c in cs if len(c)>=8]
    downs=sorted([c for c in cs if len(c)<8], key=lambda c:H-1-max(y for y,x in c)-min(y for y,x in c))
    occ=set()
    for c in ups:
        top=min(y for y,x in c)
        for (y,x) in c: out[y-top][x]=g[y][x]
        occ.update((y-top,x) for y,x in c)
    for c in downs:
        cur=set(c); val=g[list(cur)[0][0]][list(cur)[0][1]]
        step=0
        while True:
            nxt={(y+1,x) for y,x in cur}
            if any(y>=H or (y,x) in occ for y,x in nxt): break
            for (y,x) in nxt: out[y][x]=val; occ.add((y,x))
            cur=nxt;step+=1
    return out

# Rule confirmed by manual trace: each component slides toward its nearer horizontal edge,
# sliding cell-by-cell until its bounding box would exit the grid or hit an already-settled cell.
# Ordering that matched demo output: bigs (>=8) slide up, tied by smaller top-first; smalls (<8) slide down,
# orderd so far-fallers settle before closers so they don't pile on. Key insight from demo:
# - small 8a (rows2-4) ended rows3-5?? NO — demo output shows small 8 at rows13-15. 
# Actual verified observation: ALL comps in demo output end at their NEAREST edge:
#   2(top gap3)<down(9)->up rows0-3; 3a(up 4 down 9)->up rows0-2; 3b(down4)->down rows13-15;
#   8a: up2 vs down13 -> up? but output has 8a at rows13-15!! Contradiction... unless 8a's "nearest" is bottom?
# Recheck demo output 8 positions: 8 comps OUT: rows0-2 cols12-15 (10 cells) and rows13-15 cols12-15 (6).
# IN: 8 comps: rows2-4 cols12-15 (6) and rows10-12 cols12-15 (10).
# So 10-cell (dist top10, bot3) went UP to rows0-2 (moved -10); 6-cell (dist top2, bot13) went DOWN to rows13-15 (+11).
# So direction = SIZE based, NOT distance! Size>=8 up, size<8 down. 1a(7) went down (+10->rows10-12, STOPPED 3 above bottom!).
# Why did 1a stop at rows10-12? Because the small 3-comp (5 cells) settled rows13-15 cols0-2 FIRST, and 1a falling hit (13,1)?
# Wait 1a cols0-1, 3b cols0-2: overlap cols0-1! If 3b settled first occupying (13,1),(14,0..2),(15,1), 1a falling down hits (13,1) -> stacks at rows10-12 touching. YES.
# And 1b (rows8-11) fell to rows12-15 touching bottom ✓ (cols5-9 no blocker). 8a fell to bottom rows13-15 (cols14-16? cols12-15... wait small8 cells cols12-15 rows2-4; bottom rows13-15 cols12-15 ✓).
# So algorithm: smalls fall in order of travel distance ASCENDING (so closer ones settle first onto stack); bigs slide up, tie by smaller top first. Verify on demo.
def solve(g):
    H=len(g);W=len(g[0]);out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    cs=comps_of(g)
    ups=sorted([c for c in cs if len(c)>=8],key=lambda c:min(y for y,x in c))
    downs=sorted([c for c in cs if len(c)<8],key=lambda c:H-1-max(y for y,x in c)-min(y for y,x in c))
    # place bigs directly at top
    for c in ups:
        top=min(y for y,x in c)
        for (y,x) in c: out[y-top][x]=g[y][x]
    # occ from ups
    occ={(y,x) for y in range(H) for x in range(W) if out[y][x]}
    for c in downs:
        val=g[list(c)[0][0]][list(c)[0][1]]
        cur=set(c)
        while True:
            nxt={(y+1,x) for y,x in cur}
            if any(y>=H or (y,x) in occ for y,x in nxt): break
            for (y,x) in nxt: out[y][x]=val; occ.add((y,x))
            cur=nxt
    return out

def solve(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cs=comps_of(I)
    sizes=[len(c) for c in cs]
    avg=sum(sizes)/len(sizes)
    O=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for c in cs:
        cells=sorted(c)
        y0=min(y for y,x in cells); h=max(y for y,x in cells)-y0+1
        top = 0 if len(c)>avg else H-h   # large -> float to top; small -> sink to bottom
        for y,x in cells:
            ny=y-y0+top
            assert 0<=ny<H and 0<=x<W
            O[ny][x]=I[y][x]
    return O
print('demo match:', solve(I3)==O3)

def solve(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cs=comps_of(I)
    sizes=[len(c) for c in cs]
    avg=sum(sizes)/len(sizes)
    O=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for c in cs:
        cells=sorted(c)
        y0=min(y for y,x in cells); h=max(y for y,x in cells)-y0+1
        if len(c)>avg: top=0   # floats to TOP
        else:            top=H-h  # sinks to BOTTOM (bottom row at H-1)

def solve(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    ci=Counter(x for r in I for x in r)
    bg=max(ci,key=lambda v:ci[v])
    cs=comps(I,bg)
    sizes=[len(c) for c in cs]
    avg=sum(sizes)/len(sizes)
    O=[[bg]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for c in cs:
        cells=sorted(c)
        y0=min(y for y,x in cells); h=max(y for y,x in cells)-y0+1
        top = 0 if len(c)>avg else H-h   # large -> TOP; small -> bottom-anchored
        for y,x in cells:
            ny=y-y0+top
            assert 0<=ny<H and 0<=x<W
            O[ny][x]=I[y][x]
    return O

from collections import Counter
def comps(I,bg):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0]); seen=[[False]*W for _ in range(H)]; out=[]
    for y in range(H):
        for x in range(W):
            if I[y][x]!=bg and not seen[y][x]:
                c=[(y,x)]; seen[y][x]=True
                for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    ny,nx=y+dy,x+dx
                    if 0<=ny<H and 0<=nx<W and I[ny][nx]!=bg and not seen[ny][nx]:
                        seen[ny][nx]=True; c.append((ny,nx))
                out.append(c)
    return out

from collections import Counter
def solve(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    ci=Counter(x for r in I for x in r)
    bg=max(ci,key=lambda v:ci[v])
    cs=comps(I,bg)
    sizes=[len(c) for c in cs]
    avg=sum(sizes)/len(sizes)
    O=[[bg]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for c in cs:
        cells=sorted(c)
        y0=min(y for y,x in cells); hh=max(y for y,x in cells)-y0+1
        top = 0 if len(c)>avg else H-hh
        for y,x in cells:
            ny=y-y0+top
            assert 0<=ny<H and 0<=x<W
            O[ny][x]=I[y][x]
    return O
